event.summary: Restart can overlap a surviving old agent when startup tmux shutdown fails; explicitly accepted
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: If this release cannot end an old tmux server at startup, Restart may launch a second agent in the same working directory beside the first. Details: the assigned patch removes the tmux-owner and unusable-server restart refusals around core.rs:12377–12418; reload gives old-kind rows no terminal, so restart has no live agent to probe. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2924–2927 explicitly says: ‘A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)’. Suggested bucket: highest if concurrent agents overwrite user work; could-be-highest: yes, but that loss route is not established here. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance of the overlap; source tracing of reload/startup still pending. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance quoted above, for independent check; not a reportable bug unless implementation exceeds that acceptance. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveats: source-only, no observed execution; subsequent analysis must verify startup/reload implementation and whether host-only guards remain intact.

event.summary: Old-terminal fallback is explicitly accepted; a startup failure alone does not establish duplicate Restart
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; fallback introduced within the pinned range in dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: the specification accepts that an old agent left alive by retirement could run beside a later Restart, potentially allowing concurrent agents to overwrite user work. Preserve that original strongest consequence, but the earlier description of an established overlapping-agent route was too strong: startup failure alone does not establish successful Restart beside a survivor. Checks: core.rs:12377–12384 probes the held terminal; :12414–12417 settles outstanding host starts; :12472–12484 performs a fresh reap with the recorded scope, AgentOnly and ScopeKillFailure::Refuse before relaunching. Direct discovery-pass checks of sweep.rs:247–260 confirm AgentOnly selects current-agent and legacy session-only markers. :1448–1562 checks recorded scopes, keeps the portable sweep on uncertain containment and returns Err on unconfirmed recorded scopes or failed sweep. The source does not simply skip ordinary marker-readable or recorded-scoped old agents because no terminal runtime is held. old_terminals.rs:296–356 can leave old processes after its bounded startup attempt; that does not exempt them from the later fresh reap. A duplicate after a successful reap needs a survivor outside every successful selector: no usable recorded scope, no retained explicit root, and no readable matching marker (the environment-scrubbed/non-dumpable/platform-binary residual described in sweep.rs:263–307). This pass has not established a concrete ordinary resumable agent that has that shape; repository source does not establish the external installed agent's surviving process/environment shape. Platform/agent source or a retained trace of that shape would settle that remaining runtime premise; no reproduction was requested or run. Confidence: confirmed fallback policy and fresh-cleanup control flow; duplicate/work-loss runtime route not established. Suggested bucket: preserve prior high proposal and could-be-highest work-loss consequence for independent judgment; this revision corrects route certainty, not an accepted lowering or drop. proposed_drop: exact SPEC_impl.md:2924–2927 acceptance, ‘A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)’. No parent drop or lowering accepted. possible_cover: supplied neighbour g109/c1 and g007/f1 cover this same fallback and fresh-reap limitation. Material caveats: g007/c4 and g128/l1 concern later Delete consent over hidden live tabs/agents, which this Restart acceptance does not settle; g111/l1 concerns removal following moved subdirectories into a retained borrower's checkout, a separate work-loss route not covered by permission to leave an old agent alive. g033 warning and g004/g071 survival-guidance concerns remain distinct. Source/contract analysis only; no execution observation. The explicit policy is retained as a finding with proposed_drop for independent checking, with its original strongest consequences and exact basis preserved.

event.summary: Removing tmux tab enumeration does not let Delete omit historical tab cleanup
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether deleting an upgraded session can leave its old terminal-tab jobs running because this patch stops enumerating tmux tabs. Details: core.rs:13418–13430 returns every held host tab, including exited ones, with its scope selection; completeness is false for a missing terminal or any post-first-generation session. teardown.rs:402–423 uses that result to require the portable sweep and adds scopes from SessionHosts too; lines 435–459 independently enumerate both tab and launch scope globs. Thus the removed inventory does not become proof that all old tabs were contained. Host placeholders remain listed for Stop (host_tabs.rs:180–188, 271–277), and guarded Delete checks SessionHosts::untold before and after counting (core.rs:13348–13369; session_hosts.rs:587–607). SPEC.md:2083–2086 requires retaining the sweep for incomplete discovery; SPEC_impl.md:2917–2920 explicitly states: ‘what cannot be attributed to an old tab is left for the session's Delete, which sweeps the whole session’. Suggested bucket: other for the considered cleanup omission, not established. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed refutation through callers and scope/sweep fallback. proposed_drop: source refutes omission of historical tab cleanup; exact contract text quoted above. possible_cover: none. Caveats: source-only; no runtime test or reproduction performed. This does not retract c1's separate accepted surviving-old-agent consequence.

That does not establish that a no-live Delete is authorized to stop hidden live old tabs or agents. Original record: core.rs:13418–13430 returns every held host tab, exited ones included, with containment completeness false for missing terminals or later-generation sessions; teardown.rs:402–459 retains the portable sweep and independently enumerates tab/launch scopes. The alleged cleanup omission was therefore not established. Suggested bucket for that original candidate: other; could-be-highest for a distinct consent/work-loss route is now explicit, as supplied by g007/c4 and g128/l1, not dismissed by c2. Therefore the old cleanup refutation must not be read as a consent refutation. The independent records establish their complete UI/guard/WholeSession routes; no duplicate new local ID is created for known interface issues. Exact competing consent text, SPEC.md:2048, ‘a destructive confirmation authorizes only what the prompt the user answered said would happen’; :2054–2056 says a no-live Delete ‘is refused if the agent or any terminal tab is running’. Original exact cleanup acceptance, SPEC_impl.md:2917–2920, ‘what cannot be attributed to an old tab is left for the session's Delete, which sweeps the whole session’, remains preserved, but does not expressly waive that guard. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of missing cleanup; source-supported distinction from the supplied highest consent findings, no observed execution. proposed_drop: source refutation only for c2's missing-cleanup claim, not for g007/c4 or g128/l1. No parent drop/lowering accepted. possible_cover: g007/c4 owns the hidden-live-old-tab consent route; g128/l1 owns the surviving-old-agent consent route; both are distinct from c1's accepted duplicate-Restart residual. event.summary: Restart no longer needs an external output-client reap barrier
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing Restart's output-cleanup failure path can leave an old viewer streaming or let cleanup hang behind a stalled viewer. Details: core.rs:13227–13252 removes only the agent attachment, requests its shutdown, then joins its forwarder before notifying the viewer. The replacement is an in-process GridSender: grid_stream.rs:937–963 selects shutdown against the entire stream future, so shutdown cancels a blocked send; report_forwarder_end is a synchronous dispatch, not an awaited network send. The old external tmux output-client process and its reap requirement no longer exist on this path. HostAttach's owned input pump is cancelled on drop (grid_stream.rs:1169–1176), so the discarded attachment does not retain input delivery into the new terminal; it is tied to the old HostTerminal. SPEC_impl.md:2376–2377 says: ‘A viewer attached to the old host is detached before the relaunch ("session restarted") and attaches again to the new host's grid stream; nothing streams from the old host afterwards.’ Suggested bucket: other for the considered cleanup regression, refuted. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed by source. proposed_drop: replacement holds no external process and the shutdown branch cancels the whole output future, preserving the quoted contract. possible_cover: none. Caveats: source-only; no runtime test or reproduction performed.
